# Part 2 – A Business Forecasting Horse Race: ARIMA vs. ETS

Loading librarie needed for this assignment. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(fpp3)
library(BVAR)
```

### 2.1. The Data

Installing the data for the project and loading it form the data folder. 

```{r}
liquor_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/MRTSSM4453USN.csv",
  na = ".",
  col_types = cols(
    observation_date = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    MRTSSM4453USN = col_double()
  )
)

liquor <- liquor_raw |>
  transmute(Month = yearmonth(observation_date), sales = MRTSSM4453USN) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month) |>
  filter(Month <= yearmonth("2019 Dec"))

has_gaps(liquor)
```

### 2.1b - Use autoplot

Autoplot of sales. 

```{r}
liquor |> autoplot(sales) + 
  labs(title = "Liquour Sales")
```

Seasonal plot of log(sales)

```{r}
liquor |> gg_season(log(sales)) + 
  labs(title = "Seasonal log(sales) of Liquour")
```

In a few sentences: describe the trend and the seasonal pattern. Which months are high and which are low? Do the seasonal swings grow with the level of the series, and what does that suggest about using logs?

**Response:** 

The general trend is upwards. The lowest months are Jan/Feb and highest months are Nov/Dec. The seasonal swings do grow wiht the level of the series which means that logs can help us unmask actual behavior. 


## 2.2. Fit Both Models 

### 2.2a. 

```{r}
liquor_fit <- liquor |>
  model(arima = ARIMA(log(sales)),
        ets   = ETS(log(sales)))

liquor_fit |> select(arima) |> report()
liquor_fit |> select(ets) |> report()
```

Which specification was chosen for each model? In words: what does the chosen ARIMA say about how the series was differenced? What do the three letters of the chosen ETS say about its error, trend, and seasonal components?
